_comment: The citation spine. Every processed record carries a source_id that resolves here. Licence and attribution live here once, so they cannot be forgotten at render time. `redistribution` is load-bearing: the build refuses to render series from a source marked 'prohibited'.

epoch-notable-models.name: Notable AI Models
epoch-notable-models.attribution: Epoch AI, "Notable AI Models". Licensed CC BY 4.0.
epoch-notable-models.caveats: Inclusion is editorial ("notability criteria"), not exhaustive. Compute figures are frequently estimates; check the per-row confidence and notes columns before treating any value as measured.

epoch-benchmarks.name: AI Benchmarking Hub
epoch-benchmarks.attribution: Epoch AI, "AI Benchmarking Hub". Licensed CC BY 4.0.
epoch-benchmarks.caveats: Mixes Epoch's own evaluation runs with externally reported scores; these are not strictly comparable. Benchmark questions themselves remain the property of their creators and are not redistributed here. External rows retain their original licensing.

epoch-gpu-clusters.name: GPU Clusters
epoch-gpu-clusters.attribution: Epoch AI, "GPU Clusters". Licensed CC BY 4.0.
epoch-gpu-clusters.caveats: Compiled from public reporting; each row carries a certainty flag ranging from confirmed to speculative. Chinese clusters are systematically less well documented than US ones, so country totals understate opacity as much as they measure capacity.

epoch-ml-hardware.name: Machine Learning Hardware
epoch-ml-hardware.attribution: Epoch AI, "Machine Learning Hardware". Licensed CC BY 4.0.
epoch-ml-hardware.caveats: Peak theoretical throughput, not achieved throughput. Real utilisation is typically a fraction of these figures.

microsoft-ai-diffusion.name: AI Diffusion Report: AI User Share
microsoft-ai-diffusion.attribution: Microsoft AI for Good Lab, "AI Diffusion Report". MIT licence.
microsoft-ai-diffusion.caveats: Derived from anonymised Microsoft telemetry, then adjusted for OS/device market share, internet penetration and a modelled mobile-to-desktop ratio. It therefore measures Microsoft-visible AI use, scaled, not observed total AI use. Systematically less reliable where Microsoft platform share is low, and it cannot see AI embedded in products users do not recognise as AI.

anthropic-economic-index.name: Anthropic Economic Index
anthropic-economic-index.attribution: Anthropic, "Anthropic Economic Index". Licensed CC BY 4.0.
anthropic-economic-index.caveats: Claude usage only, and only consumer-tier accounts. Skews heavily toward English-speaking, developer-dense markets. Usable as one signal of AI use; misleading as a measure of it.

owid.name: Our World in Data AI charts
owid.attribution: Our World in Data. Licensed CC BY 4.0. Underlying data retains its original source's terms.
owid.caveats: OWID re-publishes third-party data. The upstream source is named in each chart's .metadata.json and must be credited alongside OWID. Requires following HTTP redirects, else the response body is empty.

lmarena.name: Arena Leaderboard Dataset
lmarena.attribution: LMArena, "Arena Leaderboard Dataset". Licensed CC BY 4.0.
lmarena.caveats: Human preference on self-selected prompts from a self-selected user population. Measures which answer people prefer, which is not the same as which answer is correct. Style-controlled variants exist and should be preferred.

us-federal-register.name: Federal Register API
us-federal-register.publisher: US Office of the Federal Register
us-federal-register.attribution: US Office of the Federal Register. US Government work, public domain.
us-federal-register.caveats: Full-text keyword matching on "artificial intelligence" returns documents that merely mention AI in passing. Requires topical filtering before display.

gov-uk.name: GOV.UK news and communications
gov-uk.attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
gov-uk.caveats: Keyword-filtered search feed, so relevance varies. Departmental press releases are political communications, not neutral descriptions of policy.

ec-digital-strategy.name: Shaping Europe's digital future
ec-digital-strategy.attribution: © European Union, 1995-2026. Reuse authorised under Decision 2011/833/EU.
ec-digital-strategy.caveats: Covers all EU digital policy, not only AI; requires topical filtering. Reuse decision does not extend to third-party material or EU logos.

nist.name: NIST news
nist.publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology
nist.attribution: US National Institute of Standards and Technology. US Government work, public domain.
nist.caveats: Covers all of NIST's remit; AI is a small fraction. Requires topical filtering.

ai-incident-database.name: AI Incident Database
ai-incident-database.attribution: AI Incident Database, Responsible AI Collaborative. Licensed ODbL 1.0.
ai-incident-database.caveats: ODbL share-alike: we display incidents but must NOT publish a derived database dump without licensing it alike. Their GraphQL API is origin-locked, so weekly tarball snapshots are the only route. Incidents are reported, not sampled - coverage reflects media attention, not incidence.

governance-readiness-index.name: AI Governance Readiness Index
governance-readiness-index.attribution: AI Safety Index, "AI Governance Readiness Index". Licensed CC BY 4.0.
governance-readiness-index.caveats: Our own editorial coding from primary legal sources, not an objective measurement. Every score cites a specific instrument and article. "Readiness" means the machinery exists to govern AI. It is emphatically not a judgement that the resulting rules are good, proportionate, or well enforced.

artificial-analysis.name: Artificial Analysis
artificial-analysis.caveats: RULED OUT. The free API tier is internal-use only and forbids redistribution. Registered here so the build fails loudly if anyone ever wires it into a rendered series. Link out to them instead.

stanford-ai-index.name: AI Index Report
stanford-ai-index.attribution: Stanford HAI, "AI Index Report 2026". Licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
stanford-ai-index.caveats: RULED OUT for charting. No-derivatives means we may not re-plot their figures or restyle their data. Cite, link, and quote sparingly only.
